sentences.en: Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about microbes
sentences.zh: 温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。

sentences.en: Microbes, most of them bacteria, have populated this planet since long before animal life developed and they will outlive us.
sentences.zh: 早在动物出现之前很久，微生物就已遍布地球，而且它们还会比我们存续得更久。微生物中大多数是细菌。

sentences.en: Invisible to the naked eye, they are ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 它们虽肉眼不可见，却无处不在。

sentences.en: They inhabit the soil, air, rocks and water and are present within every form of life, from seaweed and coral to dogs and humans.
sentences.zh: 它们生活在土壤、空气、岩石和水中，也存在于每一种生物体内，从海藻、珊瑚到狗和人，无一例外。

sentences.en: And, as Yong explains in his utterly absorbing and hugely important book, we mess with them at our peril.
sentences.zh: 而正如扬在这本引人入胜又极为重要的书里所说，随便干预微生物，我们自己就要承担风险。

sentences.en: Every species has its own colony of microbes, called a ‘microbiome’, and these microbes vary not only between species but also between individuals and within different parts of each individual.
sentences.zh: 每个物种都有自己的微生物群，称作“微生物组”。这些微生物不仅因物种而异，同一物种的不同个体之间、同一个体的不同部位之间也有差别。

sentences.en: What is amazing is that while the number of human cells in the average person is about 30 trillion, the number of microbial ones is higher — about 39 trillion.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，平均每个人体内约有30万亿个人体细胞，微生物细胞还要多，约有39万亿个。

sentences.en: At best, Yong informs us, we are only 50 per cent human.
sentences.zh: 扬告诉我们，我们顶多只有一半算是人。

sentences.en: Indeed, some scientists even suggest we should think of each species and its microbes as a single unit, dubbed a ‘holobiont’.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些科学家甚至主张，把每个物种及其共生微生物看作一个整体，称为“全生物体”。

sentences.en: In each human there are microbes that live only in the stomach, the mouth or the armpit and by and large they do so peacefully.
sentences.zh: 每个人体内都有些微生物只生活在胃里、口腔里或腋下，而且总的来说都相安无事。

sentences.en: So ‘bad’ microbes are just microbes out of context.
sentences.zh: 因此，所谓“坏”微生物，不过是出现在了不合适环境中的微生物。

sentences.en: Microbes that sit contentedly in the human gut (where there are more microbes than there are stars in the galaxy) can become deadly if they find their way into the bloodstream.
sentences.zh: 有些微生物在人的肠道中安然栖居，那里微生物的数量比银河系里的恒星还多；一旦它们进入血液，却可能致命。

sentences.en: These communities are constantly changing too.
sentences.zh: 这些微生物群落也一直在变化。

sentences.en: The right hand shares just one sixth of its microbes with the left hand.
sentences.zh: 右手上的微生物中，仅六分之一也是左手上有的。

sentences.en: And, of course, we are surrounded by microbes.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们四周也遍布微生物。

sentences.en: Every time we eat, we swallow a million microbes in each gram of food; we are continually swapping microbes with other humans, pets and the world at large.
sentences.zh: 每次进食，我们吃下的每克食物都带有一百万个微生物；我们也在不断地与其他人、宠物和周围整个世界交换微生物。

sentences.en: It’s a fascinating topic and Yong, a young British science journalist, is an extraordinarily adept guide.
sentences.zh: 这是个令人着迷的话题，而年轻的英国科学记者扬是一位格外称职的向导。

sentences.en: Writing with lightness and panache, he has a knack of explaining complex science in terms that are both easy to understand and totally enthralling.
sentences.zh: 他的笔调轻快，文采飞扬，尤其善于把复杂的科学知识讲得通俗易懂又扣人心弦。

sentences.en: Yong is on a mission.
sentences.zh: 扬写这本书有一个明确的目标。

sentences.en: Leading us gently by the hand, he takes us into the world of microbes — a bizarre, alien planet — in a bid to persuade us to love them as much as he does.
sentences.zh: 他轻轻牵着我们的手，领我们走进微生物世界。这是一个奇异而陌生的星球，而他想让我们像他一样爱上微生物。

sentences.en: By the end, we do.
sentences.zh: 读到最后，我们果真爱上了它们。

sentences.en: For most of human history we had no idea that microbes existed.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史上的大部分时间里，我们根本不知道微生物的存在。

sentences.en: The first man to see these extraordinarily potent creatures was a Dutch lens-maker called Antony van Leeuwenhoek in the 1670s.
sentences.zh: 17世纪70年代，一位名叫安东尼·范·列文虎克的荷兰镜片匠，成为第一个看到这些影响非凡的生物的人。

sentences.en: Using microscopes of his own design that could magnify up to 270 times, he examined a drop of water from a nearby lake and found it teeming with tiny creatures he called ‘animalcules’.
sentences.zh: 他用自己设计的显微镜观察附近湖里的一滴水，显微镜最高可放大270倍。他发现水里满是微小的生物，便称它们为“微小动物”。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until nearly two hundred years later that the research of French biologist Louis Pasteur indicated that some microbes caused disease.
sentences.zh: 直到将近两百年后，法国生物学家路易·巴斯德的研究才表明，有些微生物会引起疾病。

sentences.en: It was Pasteur’s ‘germ theory’ that gave bacteria the poor image that endures today.
sentences.zh: 正是巴斯德的“病菌学说”让细菌背上了坏名声，这种印象一直延续到今天。

sentences.en: Yong’s book is in many ways a plea for microbial tolerance, pointing out that while fewer than one hundred species of bacteria bring disease, many thousands more play a vital role in maintaining our health.
sentences.zh: 从许多方面看，扬的书都在呼吁人们宽容对待微生物。他指出，致病细菌不足一百种，而帮助我们维持健康的细菌却有成千上万种。

sentences.en: The book also acknowledges that our attitude towards bacteria is not a simple one.
sentences.zh: 这本书也承认，我们对细菌的态度并不简单。

sentences.en: We tend to see the dangers posed by bacteria, yet at the same time we are sold yoghurts and drinks that supposedly nurture ‘friendly’ bacteria.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会注意到细菌带来的危险，可与此同时，商家又向我们推销据说能滋养“友好”细菌的酸奶和饮品。

sentences.en: In reality, says Yong, bacteria should not be viewed as either friends or foes, villains or heroes.
sentences.zh: 扬说，实际上，不宜把细菌简单看成朋友或敌人、反派或英雄。

sentences.en: Instead we should realise we have a symbiotic relationship, that can be mutually beneficial or mutually destructive.
sentences.zh: 我们应该认识到，人和细菌是共生的；这种关系既可能对双方有益，也可能彼此有害。

sentences.en: What then do these millions of organisms do?
sentences.zh: 那么，这数以百万计的生物究竟有何作用？

sentences.en: The answer is pretty much everything.
sentences.zh: 答案是，它们几乎什么都做。

sentences.en: New research is now unravelling the ways in which bacteria aid digestion, regulate our immune systems, eliminate toxins, produce vitamins, affect our behaviour and even combat obesity.
sentences.zh: 新的研究正在揭示细菌如何帮助消化、调节免疫系统、清除毒素，以及如何制造维生素、影响我们的行为，甚至对抗肥胖。

sentences.en: ‘They actually help us become who we are,’ says Yong.
sentences.zh: “它们实际上帮助我们成了今天的我们，”扬说。

sentences.en: But we are facing a growing problem.
sentences.zh: 但我们正面临一个日益严重的问题。

sentences.en: Our obsession with hygiene, our overuse of antibiotics and our unhealthy, low-fibre diets are disrupting the bacterial balance and may be responsible for soaring rates of allergies and immune problems, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
sentences.zh: 对卫生的过分执着、滥用抗生素，以及不健康的低纤维饮食，正在破坏我们体内的细菌平衡，也可能是过敏及炎症性肠病（IBD）等免疫问题发生率飙升的原因。

sentences.en: The most recent research actually turns accepted norms upside down.
sentences.zh: 最新的研究其实颠覆了人们过去普遍接受的观念。

sentences.en: For example, there are studies indicating that the excessive use of household detergents and antibacterial products actually destroys the microbes that normally keep the more dangerous germs at bay.
sentences.zh: 例如，有研究表明，过度使用家用清洁剂和抗菌产品，反而会消灭那些通常能遏制更危险病菌的微生物。

sentences.en: Other studies show that keeping a dog as a pet gives children early exposure to a diverse range of bacteria, which may help protect them against allergies later.
sentences.zh: 另一些研究显示，家里养狗让孩子很早就能接触到多种多样的细菌，这或许有助于防止他们日后出现过敏。

sentences.en: The readers of Yong’s book must be prepared for a decidedly unglamorous world.
sentences.zh: 读扬这本书的人要有心理准备：书中描绘的世界实在不怎么光鲜。

sentences.en: Among the less appealing case studies is one about a fungus that is wiping out entire populations of frogs and that can be halted by a rare microbial bacterium.
sentences.zh: 其中一些案例读来没那么讨喜。一个案例讲的是一种真菌：它正使青蛙种群整群消亡，而一种罕见的细菌可以遏止这种真菌。

sentences.en: Another is about squid that carry luminescent bacteria that protect them against predators.
sentences.zh: 另一个案例讲的是鱿鱼：它们身上带有能发光的细菌，能够借此躲避捕食者。

sentences.en: However, if you can overcome your distaste for some of the investigations, the reasons for Yong’s enthusiasm become clear.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果你能克服对某些研究的反感，就不难理解扬为何如此热衷于这个领域。

sentences.en: The microbial world is a place of wonder.
sentences.zh: 微生物世界令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Already, in an attempt to stop mosquitoes spreading dengue fever — a disease that infects 400 million people a year — mosquitoes are being loaded with a bacterium to block the disease.
sentences.zh: 为防止蚊子传播登革热，已经有人让蚊子携带一种能阻断传播的细菌。登革热每年会导致四亿人感染。

sentences.en: In the future, our ability to manipulate microbes means we could construct buildings with useful microbes built into their walls to fight off infections.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，我们对微生物的调控能力意味着，我们也许能建造这样的楼宇，把有益的微生物纳入墙体来抵御感染。

sentences.en: Just imagine a neonatal hospital ward coated in a specially mixed cocktail of microbes so that babies get the best start in life.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，在医院的新生儿病房里，病房内的表面覆盖着专门调配的多种微生物，好让婴儿获得最佳的人生开端。

options.B: The risk they pose has been exaggerated

options.C: the average individual has more microbial cells than human ones.
